description: We are a team of developers, researchers, and creators passionate about space history and interactive media. For the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, we are building a narrative-driven platform that turns dormant landers, rovers, and equipment on the Moon and Mars into compelling educational stories for students and space enthusiasts.
summary:
NEBIX - Abandoned but Not Forgotten

Our project is an interactive educational website that explores the stories and importance of human-made space equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions ended.

We developed a website featuring five historical space objects, including lunar landers, a rover, and Mars missions. Through mission stories, timelines, images, and an interactive quiz, visitors can discover why these machines were sent, what they achieved, and what remains of them today.

Our project addresses the challenge by raising awareness of the scientific, historical, and technological value of abandoned space equipment. Rather than viewing these objects as forgotten debris, we highlight them as important milestones in space exploration. We believe preserving their stories helps people especially students and space enthusiasts better understand humanity's journey beyond Earth and appreciate the legacy of past missions.
details:
Our project, Abandoned but Not Forgotten, is an interactive educational website designed to raise awareness about human-made space equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions ended.

The website allows visitors to explore five historical space objects through dedicated stories that explain their original missions, important discoveries, achievements, and current status. Each object is presented using images, clear information, and timelines to make its history easier to understand. We also included an interactive quiz to help visitors test what they have learned.

The main benefit of our project is making space history more accessible and engaging, especially for students and people interested in space exploration. Its intended impact is to encourage people to recognize that these objects are not simply abandoned machines, but valuable parts of humanity's scientific and technological history.

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with no frameworks, databases, or external APIs. The project is hosted on GitHub Pages, and its information is organized in separate JavaScript data and functionality files. We used Visual Studio Code for development.

The creative aspect of our project is the way it turns historical information into an interactive experience. Instead of presenting a simple list of abandoned equipment, we tell the stories behind each object and connect them to the wider history of space exploration.

During development, our team considered accuracy, simplicity, accessibility, visual design, and ease of navigation. We also chose to keep the website lightweight and locally structured, so visitors can explore its content without depending on external APIs or complicated systems.
